1. The Report Was Accidentally Paused

Open Brightline Home > Reports > Scheduled and confirm the Active toggle is set to On for your report. A paused report will show a Paused badge in gray.

Check your spam, promotions, or junk folder for emails from reports@mail.brightlinesolar.com. Adding that address to your contacts prevents future filtering.

During periods of high platform load, scheduled reports may be queued and delivered up to 4 hours after their scheduled time. If your report arrived late but eventually appeared, no action is needed.

5. Data Sync Error (Error Code RPT-4402)

If your monitoring gateway lost connectivity during the reporting window, the system may skip that delivery and log error code RPT-4402. You will receive an in-app alert under Alerts > System. The next scheduled report will generate normally once connectivity is restored.

Contact Brightline Support via Brightline Home > Help > Chat with Us and include your report name and the date of the last successful delivery. Title: Why does my loan statement balance not match what I expected?

Answer__c:
Common Reasons for an Unexpected Balance

Several factors can cause your closing balance to differ from what you anticipated. The most frequent reasons are listed below.

1. Interest Accrues Daily

Brightline Solar loans use simple daily interest. This means interest accumulates each day based on your current principal. If your payment arrived even a few days late, additional interest will have accrued before your payment was applied, leaving a slightly higher balance than expected.

2. Payment Application Order

Payments are applied in the following order: (1) outstanding fees, (2) accrued interest, (3) principal. If you carry a late fee or returned-payment fee from a prior period, your payment reduces those charges first, and less principal is paid down than you may have anticipated.

3. Partial Payments

If you made a partial payment in the previous period, the unpaid remainder rolled forward and continued to accrue interest. See How does Brightline apply partial payments to my account balance? for details on how this works.

4. Hardship Deferral Adjustments

If you enrolled in a payment deferral through the Brightline Hardship Program, deferred amounts and any associated interest adjustments will appear as separate line items on your statement. Refer to Hardship Program Expansion: Extended Deferral (January 2026) for program terms.

What to Do Next

SituationRecommended Action
Balance seems too highReview the interest accrued and fees lines; contact support at 1-800-555-0192 if a charge appears incorrect
Balance seems too lowConfirm all expected payments were processed; check Payment History in the app
Deferral not reflectedAllow up to 5 business days after deferral approval for the statement to update

If you believe there is an error, you can open a billing dispute directly in the app under Account > Financing > Loan Statements > [Statement] > Dispute a Charge.

Title: Why does my production estimate differ from my actual output?
Summary: Explains the common reasons a system's estimated annual production may not match real-world generation figures shown in Brightline Home.
Answer__c:
Why Estimates and Actuals Sometimes Diverge

Production estimates are calculated at the time of your site survey using historical solar irradiance data, your roof's pitch and azimuth, shading analysis, and the rated output of your specific panel model. They represent a long-run average under typical conditions — not a guaranteed figure for any single year.

Common Causes of a Lower-Than-Expected Output

  • Unusual weather: A year with significantly more cloud cover, rain, or wildfire smoke than the 20-year historical average used in your estimate will reduce generation.
  • Panel soiling: Dust, pollen, bird droppings, or debris can reduce output by 3–8% if panels have not been cleaned in 12+ months.
  • Shading changes: Tree growth or new structures near your home may create shading that did not exist during your site survey.
  • Inverter or microinverter underperformance: One or more underperforming units can drag total output down. Check the Device Status tab in Brightline Home for any flagged units.
  • System degradation: Panels degrade at roughly 0.5% per year, which is already factored into multi-year estimates but can appear as a small annual shortfall.

When to Contact Support

A gap of up to 10% below the annual estimate is generally within normal variance. If your shortfall exceeds 15% and weather alone does not explain it, contact Brightline Support — a performance review ticket can be opened from Reports → Production Estimate → Request Performance Review in Brightline Home.

For details on viewing and downloading your full estimate report, see How to view and download your production estimate report. To understand how estimates are built from your site data, see Site survey scheduling — self-serve launch.

Title: Why did I receive a prorated charge on my invoice?
Summary: Prorated charges appear when your billing period starts or ends mid-month due to a plan activation, change, or cancellation.
Answer__c:
What Is a Prorated Charge?

A prorated charge covers a partial billing period rather than a full calendar month. Brightline Solar calculates your monthly monitoring, maintenance plan, or battery management fee on a 30-day cycle. When an event causes your billing period to begin or end on a day other than your normal billing date, we charge only for the days of service you actually received.

Common Reasons You May See a Prorated Charge

  • System activation mid-month: Your system went live on a day other than your regular billing date, so your first invoice covers only the days from activation through the end of that cycle.
  • Plan upgrade or downgrade: Switching between monitoring tiers (e.g., from Brightline Essential to Brightline Plus) triggers a prorated credit for unused days on the old plan and a prorated charge for days on the new plan.
  • Home sale or transfer: Service ending before a billing period closes results in a final prorated invoice for remaining days.

How the Amount Is Calculated

The formula is straightforward:

Prorated Amount = (Monthly Plan Rate ÷ 30) × Number of Active Days

For example, if your Brightline Plus plan is $24.99/month and you activated on the 11th of a 30-day cycle, you are billed for 20 days: ($24.99 ÷ 30) × 20 = $16.66.

Where to Find the Breakdown

Open the Brightline Home app, tap Account → Billing → Invoice History, and select the invoice in question. Each prorated line item shows the start date, end date, daily rate, and day count.

If you believe the dates shown are incorrect, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 within 30 days of the invoice date. For context on how charges are handled during a home sale, see Who is responsible for the solar system during the home sale closing period?

What Counts as a Partial Payment

A partial payment is any amount less than the full Statement Balance shown on your current invoice. Brightline Home accepts partial payments through the app, but your account will reflect an outstanding balance equal to the unpaid portion.

How the Remaining Balance Is Handled

The unpaid amount is carried forward to your next billing cycle and appears as a Previous Balance line item on your following invoice. You will not be charged a separate balance-transfer fee for this rollover.

Late Fees and Service Impacts

If your partial payment is received by the due date, the late-payment fee of $9.95 is waived for that cycle. However, if the total outstanding balance (current charges plus carried-over balance) remains unpaid past 30 days after the original due date, the $9.95 late fee is applied automatically. Repeated partial payments over three or more consecutive cycles may trigger an account review under Brightline's collections policy.

Monitoring Your Balance in Brightline Home

  2. Select Account Summary to see your current balance, any carried-forward amount, and the next due date.
  3. Tap Make a Payment to submit an additional payment at any time before your next statement closes.

Financial Hardship Options

If partial payments are becoming a recurring necessity, you may qualify for the Brightline Hardship Program, which offers deferred payments and reduced minimums. See Brightline Hardship Program for eligibility details.

Title: What happens during a Brightline site survey?
Summary: A site survey is a pre-installation visit where a Brightline technician evaluates your home's roof, electrical panel, and property to design your solar system.
Answer__c:
What Is a Site Survey?

A site survey is a mandatory pre-installation assessment conducted by a certified Brightline field technician before your solar system design is finalized. It typically takes 60–90 minutes, though larger homes or complex roof layouts may require up to 2 hours.

What the Technician Will Inspect

  • Roof structure: Material type (shingle, tile, metal), pitch, condition, and available surface area for panel placement.
  • Electrical panel: Current amperage rating, available breaker slots, and compatibility with your planned system size.
  • Attic access: Rafter spacing and structural integrity for mounting hardware.
  • Shading analysis: Using a calibrated solar pathfinder tool, the technician maps obstructions such as trees or neighboring structures across all daylight hours.
  • Utility meter and interconnection point: Location and accessibility for the inverter and production meter installation.

What You Should Prepare

  1. Ensure an adult (18+) is present for the full duration of the visit.
  2. Clear a 3-foot perimeter around your main electrical panel.
  3. Provide attic access if a pull-down staircase or hatch is the only entry point.
  4. Have a recent utility bill available — the technician may ask about your average monthly usage.

After the Survey

Results are uploaded to your Brightline account within 2 business days. You will receive an in-app notification in Brightline Home under My Project > Survey Results once your customized system design is ready for review.

If the technician identifies a concern (such as a roof needing repair before installation), you will receive a separate Pre-Installation Requirements notice via email and in-app alert.

Title: What documents are required for a ground-mount solar permit?

Answer__c:
Ground-Mount Permit Document Checklist

Ground-mount installations require a more extensive permit package than rooftop systems because they involve foundation work, setback reviews, and sometimes stormwater or grading approvals. Brightline prepares and submits the following on your behalf:

  • Structural engineering report – stamped by a licensed engineer, covering the racking foundation (helical piers, ballast, or concrete footings depending on your soil assessment)
  • Electrical single-line diagram – showing the AC/DC wiring path from array to your main panel or battery system
  • Site plan – scaled plot map indicating array location, property lines, setbacks, and overhead utility lines
  • Geotechnical or soil report – required by most jurisdictions when helical piers or concrete footings are used
  • Zoning compliance letter – confirming the array meets local height and setback rules

What You May Need to Provide

In some counties, the permit authority requires the homeowner of record to sign a notarized authorization form before Brightline can submit. Your project coordinator will send this via DocuSign if it applies to your jurisdiction. You may also need to provide a copy of your current property survey if one was not completed during your site assessment.

Typical Review Timeline

Once your complete document package is submitted, most jurisdictions return a decision within 15–35 business days. Complex parcels with HOA overlay districts or agricultural zoning can take up to 60 business days. You can track permit status in the Brightline Home app under My Project → Permits → Ground-Mount Permit.

Error Code for Missing Keys

If you omit an idempotency key on a required endpoint, the API returns HTTP 400 with error code ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISSING in the response body. No operation is performed.

Conflict Errors

If you reuse a key on a different endpoint or with a different request body, you will receive HTTP 409 with error code ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT. Always pair a unique key with a unique logical operation.

Answer__c:
Overview of Report Time Periods

Your production estimate report in Brightline Home (Reports → Production Estimates) is organized into three nested time horizons, each serving a different planning purpose.

Monthly Estimates

The Monthly tab shows expected kWh output for each calendar month based on your location's average solar irradiance profile. Summer months will show higher estimates than winter months. These figures update automatically if Brightline recalibrates your system model — you will see a Revised badge on any month that has been updated since your original installation estimate.

Annual Estimates

The Annual tab aggregates monthly figures into a full-year total and compares it against your actual metered production year-to-date. A green indicator means you are tracking at or above estimate; amber means 5–14% below; red means 15%+ below and may trigger a proactive support outreach from Brightline.

25-Year Projection

The 25-Year Projection tab models cumulative production across your system's expected lifespan, applying a 0.5% annual degradation rate to each successive year. This view also shows estimated lifetime savings in kWh and, where applicable, estimated utility bill offset in dollars based on the rate you provided during onboarding.

Accuracy and Revisions

  • Monthly and annual estimates carry a stated accuracy range of ±8%.
  • 25-year projections carry a wider range of ±15% due to long-term irradiance and rate uncertainty.
  • Estimates can be revised after a system expansion, panel replacement, or tariff change — you will receive an in-app notification when a revision occurs.

A co-borrower on a Brightline solar loan is a full legal party to the loan agreement — not just a cosigner. This means they have independent rights to:

  • Both parties are equally responsible for on-time payments
  • A missed payment affects both borrowers' credit profiles
  • Either borrower can be pursued for the full outstanding balance if the other defaults

What a Co-Borrower Cannot Do Unilaterally

Some actions require written consent from both parties, including removing a co-borrower from the loan, modifying loan terms, or initiating a loan transfer in connection with a home sale.

Title: What is an idempotency key and why do I need one in the Partner API?
Summary: Explains what idempotency keys are, why Brightline's Partner API requires them for certain requests, and how they protect you from duplicate operations.
Answer__c:
What Is an Idempotency Key?

An idempotency key is a unique string you generate and attach to a Partner API request so that Brightline's servers can recognize a retry of the same operation and return the original result instead of executing the action a second time. If your network request times out or drops before you receive a response, you can safely resend the exact same request with the same key and know it will not be processed twice.

When Is It Required?

Idempotency keys are mandatory on all requests that create or modify state. This includes:

  • Payment and billing operations (POST /v2/payments)
  • Webhook subscription creation (POST /v2/webhooks)
  • Battery dispatch commands (POST /v2/devices/{deviceId}/dispatch)
  • Report schedule creation (POST /v2/report-schedules)

Read-only GET requests do not require an idempotency key because fetching data is already safe to repeat.

What Happens If I Omit It?

The API returns HTTP 400 with error code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISSING and the message: "A valid Idempotency-Key header is required for this request." The request is rejected and no action is taken.

Key Format Requirements

Keys must be 8–128 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, or underscores. UUIDs (v4) are the recommended format. Keys expire from Brightline's deduplication store after 72 hours.

For related guidance on scheduling report endpoints that require idempotency keys, see How to Configure Report Schedules via the Partner API.

Title: What happens to my Brightline solar loan if my co-borrower and I separate or divorce?
Summary: Separation or divorce does not automatically change your loan agreement, and both parties remain liable until Brightline formally approves a co-borrower removal or loan refinance.
Answer__c:
Your Loan Agreement Does Not Change Automatically

A divorce decree or separation agreement is a legal document between you and your co-borrower, but it is not binding on Brightline. Until the loan is formally modified, both parties remain equally liable for all payments, regardless of what your divorce settlement specifies.

Options for Resolving the Loan

  • Co-borrower removal: Either party may submit a co-borrower removal request via Brightline Home > Account > Financing > Manage Co-Borrower. The remaining borrower must qualify for the full loan amount through a new credit review. Processing takes approximately 15–20 business days. A $75 loan modification fee applies unless waived by a Brightline financing specialist.
  • Full payoff: One party may pay off the loan in full. Request a payoff letter at least 5 business days before the intended payoff date.
  • Home sale and loan transfer: If the property is being sold, the loan may be paid off from sale proceeds or, in eligible cases, transferred to a qualified buyer.

What to Expect During Review

During the co-borrower removal review period, the account remains active and payments are still due on their normal schedule. Late payments during this period will affect both parties' credit.

Get Help

Contact Brightline Financing Support at 1-800-555-0192 (Mon–Fri, 8 AM–6 PM local time) to discuss your specific situation. See also How do I add or remove a co-borrower from my Brightline solar loan? and Payoff letter request now available in Brightline Home.

Summary: Explains why a dispute may be denied, how to appeal the decision, and alternative options like hardship assistance if you cannot pay the disputed amount.
Answer__c:
Understanding a Denied Dispute

If your dispute is denied, you will receive an email with the subject line Dispute Decision: DSP-XXXXXXXX – Not Upheld. The email includes a plain-language explanation and the specific reason code assigned by our billing team. Common denial reason codes include:

A denied dispute does not automatically trigger a late fee while an active appeal is on file. However, if the appeal is ultimately unsuccessful, standard late fees (1.5% per month) will be applied retroactively to the original due date. If paying the charge would create financial hardship, you may qualify for a payment deferral — see Brightline Hardship Program for eligibility details. Title: View Your Lifetime Production Stats in Brightline Home

Before you begin: You must be logged in to the Brightline Home app (version 4.2.0 or later) as the account owner or an authorized household member. Lifetime stats are available starting 24 hours after your system's Permission to Operate (PTO) date is recorded in your account. If your system was installed before March 2023, data is displayed from the earliest available meter reading, which may not represent day one of operation.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Dashboard on the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Tap the Reports tab at the top of the screen.
  3. Select Production Summary from the report type menu.
  4. Tap the Date Range picker and choose Lifetime from the dropdown. The picker defaults to the current calendar month.
  5. Review the summary cards that appear: Total kWh Generated, Estimated CO₂ Offset (lbs), and Estimated Bill Savings ($). Savings figures are calculated using your rate plan on file and are estimates only.

Lifetime option is grayed out: Your system's PTO date may not yet be recorded. Contact Brightline Support if it has been more than 48 hours since your system was activated.

Totals appear lower than expected: If you had a monitoring gateway replacement or a microinverter swap, a small data gap may exist. See What causes a microinverter to show offline in Brightline Home for context on data gaps caused by offline events.

Export email never arrives: Check your spam folder. If it does not arrive within 15 minutes, retry the export or review your account email address under Settings > Account Info. For help updating your email, see How do I change my email address in Brightline Home.

Title: Update Your Preferred Contact Method for Installer Communications

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap the Menu icon (☰), then select Profile.
  2. Tap Communication Preferences near the top of the Profile screen.
  3. Under the Installer Contact heading, tap Edit.

You did not receive the SMS verification code. Wait 2 minutes, then tap Resend Code. Codes expire after 10 minutes. If you still do not receive a code, confirm the number you entered is a US mobile number capable of receiving SMS — VoIP numbers are not supported for verification.

The Save Changes button is grayed out. This usually means a verification step is still pending. Check that both the phone and email fields show a green check mark before saving. Title: Retrieve Lifetime Production Stats via the Partner API
Summary: Use the Partner API's Reports endpoint to programmatically request all-time production totals for one or more customer systems.
Procedure_Body__c:
Prerequisites: You must hold a valid OAuth2 access token with the reports:read scope. Your application must be approved for the Lifetime aggregation tier in the Brightline Developer Portal (Portal > App Settings > Data Access > Aggregation Tiers). Accounts without this tier approved will receive a 403 TIER_NOT_AUTHORIZED response. Refer to your token management workflow before proceeding; see Partner API OAuth2 Token Lifetime and Error Handling Update (October 2025) for current token expiry rules.

  1. Construct a GET request to https://api.brightlinesolar.io/v2/reports/production.
  2. Set the Authorization header to Bearer <your_access_token>.
  3. Add the query parameter period=lifetime. Optionally add system_id=<id> to scope the request to a single system; omit it to return all systems your token is authorized to access.
  4. Send the request. A successful response returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing total_kwh, co2_offset_lbs, estimated_savings_usd, data_start_date, and data_end_date fields.
  5. If you need a breakdown by year, append the query parameter granularity=yearly. The response will include a periods array with one object per calendar year.
  6. Cache responses on your side for at least 1 hour. Lifetime totals update once every 6 hours on Brightline's side; polling more frequently wastes quota and may trigger rate limiting.
  7. For bulk requests covering more than 500 systems, use pagination: include page=1&page_size=500 and iterate using the next_cursor field returned in the response envelope.

Troubleshooting

HTTP 429 Too Many Requests: You have exceeded the Reports endpoint rate limit of 120 requests per minute per application. Implement exponential backoff and honor the Retry-After header. See What does error code 429 mean in the Partner API for detailed guidance.

Empty total_kwh value (returns 0 or null): The system's PTO date is not yet recorded, or the system has no meter readings older than 24 hours. Verify the system status using GET /v2/systems/{system_id}/status before retrying.

HTTP 503 or intermittent failures: The Reports service may be under maintenance. Check the Brightline API Status page and review retry strategies at How do I troubleshoot 5xx errors in the Partner API.

Mismatched totals vs. app: Confirm your token's authorized system list matches the customer's account. Discrepancies of under 2% are expected due to rounding; larger gaps should be reported to Brightline Partner Support with the response's request_id value.

Title: Resolve OAuth2 Token Errors in the Partner API
Summary: Follow these steps to diagnose and fix the most common OAuth2 authentication errors returned by the Brightline Partner API, including expired tokens, invalid client credentials, and scope mismatches.
Procedure_Body__c:
Prerequisites: You must have an active Brightline Partner account with API credentials issued from the Partner Developer Portal (portal.brightlinesolar.dev). You will need your client_id, client_secret, and the list of OAuth2 scopes your application requested at onboarding. If you are using the official SDK, ensure you are on version 2.x or later (see Partner API SDK v2 Breaking Changes – March 2026).

  1. Identify the error code. Every authentication failure returns a JSON body with an error field. Common values are OAUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED, OAUTH_INVALID_CLIENT, OAUTH_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT, and OAUTH_TOKEN_REVOKED. Note the HTTP status code alongside it (typically 401 or 403).
  2. Check token expiry (OAUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED). Access tokens issued by the Brightline authorization server are valid for 3,600 seconds (1 hour). If your integration does not cache and refresh tokens proactively, request a new token using the client_credentials grant before the current token expires. The token response includes an expires_in field you should track.
  3. Verify client credentials (OAUTH_INVALID_CLIENT). Log in to the Partner Developer Portal, navigate to Settings > API Credentials, and confirm that the client_id and client_secret in your environment match exactly. Secrets are case-sensitive and must not contain leading or trailing whitespace.
  4. Confirm scopes (OAUTH_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT). The endpoint you are calling may require a scope your application was not granted. In the Portal, go to Settings > API Credentials > Manage Scopes and compare your granted scopes against the endpoint's documentation. Submit a scope expansion request from that same page; approval typically takes 1–2 business days.
  5. Handle a revoked token (OAUTH_TOKEN_REVOKED). Tokens are revoked when a partner account is suspended, a secret is rotated, or a security event is detected. Rotating your secret in the Portal automatically invalidates all existing tokens. Generate a new secret, update your environment variables, and request a fresh token.
  6. Test with a raw HTTP request. To isolate whether the error is in your SDK or your credentials, send a direct POST to https://auth.brightlinesolar.dev/oauth2/token with the Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded header and your credentials. A successful response returns 200 OK with an access_token.
  7. Retry your original request. Attach the new token in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header and confirm you receive a 200 or 202 response.

Troubleshooting

Error persists after rotating the secret: Allow up to 60 seconds for the new secret to propagate across Brightline authorization servers before retrying. Clock skew causes repeated expiry errors: The Brightline auth server rejects tokens if your server clock differs by more than 5 minutes; synchronize your system clock using NTP. Scope expansion not reflected after approval: You must request a new token after approval — existing tokens do not inherit newly granted scopes automatically. If none of these steps resolve the issue, open a support ticket from the Portal under Help > Contact Partner Support and include the X-Request-ID header value from the failed response. For guidance on idempotency when retrying failed requests, see How Do Idempotency Keys Behave When a Partner API Request Fails or Is Retried.

Title: How long does an idempotency key stay valid in the Partner API?
Summary: Idempotency keys in the Brightline Partner API remain active for 24 hours, after which the same key can produce a new result if reused.
Answer__c:
Idempotency Key Validity Window

Every idempotency key you include in a Brightline Partner API request is stored in our deduplication cache for exactly 24 hours from the moment the request first reaches our servers. During that window, any repeat call using the identical key and endpoint will receive the original cached response—including the original HTTP status code, response body, and X-Brightline-Request-Id header—without triggering a second operation.

What Happens After 24 Hours

Once the 24-hour window closes, the key is purged from the cache. If you submit a new request using that same key after expiry, the API treats it as a brand-new request and executes the operation again. This can result in duplicate records or charges, so you should generate a fresh key for any intentional retry after the window has lapsed.

Key Format Requirements

  • Must be sent in the Idempotency-Key request header.
  • Maximum length: 128 characters.
  • Accepted format: UUID v4 (recommended) or any URL-safe alphanumeric string.
  • Keys are scoped per OAuth2 client ID—the same string used by two different clients does not conflict.

Checking Cache Status

If you need to confirm whether a key is still cached, inspect the response header X-Brightline-Idempotency-Status. A value of replayed confirms you received a cached result; original means the request was processed fresh.

For a foundational overview, see What is an idempotency key and why do I need one?

Title: How long does Brightline take to resolve an invoice dispute?
Summary: Explains the typical timeline for invoice dispute resolution, what happens at each stage, and when to expect a final decision or credit.
Answer__c:
Dispute Resolution Timeline

Once you submit a dispute through Brightline Home → Billing → Invoice History → [Invoice] → Dispute This Charge, our billing team begins review within 2 business days. The full process has three stages:

  1. Acknowledgment (within 2 business days): You'll receive an email and an in-app notification confirming your dispute reference number (format: DSP-XXXXXXXX).
  2. Active Review (up to 10 business days): A billing specialist examines your usage data, payment history, and any supporting documents you uploaded. If additional information is needed, they'll contact you via the email on your account — responding promptly keeps the clock from pausing.
  3. Decision (by business day 12): You'll be notified of the outcome in-app and by email. If the dispute is resolved in your favor, a credit or refund is applied within 5–7 business days.

While Your Dispute Is Open

The disputed amount is placed in a temporary hold status. Autopay will not process the held amount until the dispute closes, so you won't be charged twice. However, undisputed line items on the same invoice remain due on their original due date to avoid a late fee of $4.95.

Escalating a Delayed Dispute

If you haven't received a decision by business day 13, contact us at 1-800-BRIGHTLN or chat in the app with your DSP- reference number ready. For context on refund timing after a dispute is resolved in your favor, see Refund Processing Time Update. If you're concerned a dispute may be denied, review What Happens If My Invoice Dispute Is Denied.

Title: How long will a weather delay postpone my installation appointment?

Answer__c:
Typical Rescheduling Timeframes

When Brightline Solar postpones an installation due to unsafe weather conditions—such as high winds (sustained speeds above 25 mph), active precipitation, or lightning within 10 miles of the job site—our scheduling team begins rebooking affected appointments within 1 business day of the original date. In most cases, your new appointment will fall within 5–14 calendar days of the cancelled visit, depending on crew availability and local permit validity.

Factors That Can Extend the Wait

  • Regional weather patterns: Prolonged storm systems (e.g., multi-day rain events) may push your slot further out if multiple crews are affected simultaneously.
  • Permit expiration windows: If your installation permit expires within 30 days of the delay, a Brightline permit coordinator will contact you separately to discuss extension options before rescheduling.
  • Roof-access requirements: Delays may be longer if your property requires a scheduled access window. Review how to grant roof access for a scheduled service visit to ensure your access credentials remain active.
  • Equipment staging: Pre-staged equipment at a local warehouse is held for up to 21 days before it must be reassigned to another job.

What to Expect Next

You will receive an automated push notification and email from the Brightline Home app with your new proposed appointment time. You can accept, request a different date, or view delay status details directly in the app. For step-by-step status tracking, see how to check the status of a weather-delayed appointment in Brightline Home.

Title: Identify and Dismiss a False Alarm in Brightline Home
Summary: Learn how to recognize when an alert in the Brightline Home app is a false alarm and how to dismiss it without affecting your system's alert history.
Procedure_Body__c:
Before you begin: You will need the Brightline Home app (version 4.2.0 or later) installed on your mobile device and an active internet connection. Only the account owner or an authorized household member with Alert permissions can dismiss alerts.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Alerts in the bottom navigation bar. Active alerts appear at the top under Needs Attention.
  2. Tap the alert you want to investigate. Review the alert detail screen, which shows the alert code (for example, ALT-204: Low Production Warning), the time it triggered, and the affected component.
  3. Tap Check System Status on the alert detail screen. The app polls your inverter and gateway in real time. If all readings return green within 60 seconds, the alert is likely a false alarm caused by a brief communication dropout or a transient grid fluctuation.
  4. Scroll down to the Possible Causes section. Look for entries labeled Transient — no action required. These are pre-classified false-alarm patterns based on your system's telemetry history.
  5. Tap Mark as False Alarm, then select a reason from the dropdown (options include Temporary shading, Grid momentary outage, App connectivity gap, or Other). Adding a brief note is optional but helps Brightline improve alert accuracy.
  6. Tap Confirm Dismiss. The alert moves to Alert History with a False Alarm label and is excluded from your monthly Alert Summary report.

Troubleshooting

The Mark as False Alarm button is grayed out. This occurs when an alert carries a Critical severity flag (code prefix ALT-5xx). Critical alerts cannot be self-dismissed; contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 so a technician can verify the issue before it is cleared.

The system status check times out. If the real-time poll does not complete within 90 seconds, your gateway may be offline. Title: Paginate Through Large Result Sets in the Partner API
Summary: Step-by-step instructions for using the Partner API's cursor-based pagination to retrieve complete multi-page responses without duplicating or skipping records.
Procedure_Body__c:
Prerequisites: You must have a valid OAuth2 access token with at least the read:sites scope. Pagination applies to any Partner API collection endpoint that returns a pagination object in its response envelope, including /v2/sites, /v2/reports, and /v2/alerts. Confirm your client library is up to date; see Partner API SDK Launch – Python & Node for version requirements.

  1. Make your initial request to the desired collection endpoint. Include the query parameter page_size (integer, 1–500; default 100) to control how many records are returned per page. Example: GET /v2/sites?page_size=200.
  2. Inspect the response envelope's pagination object. It contains three fields: total_records (total matching items), next_cursor (an opaque Base64 string), and has_more (boolean).
  3. If has_more is true, append the cursor query parameter to your next request using the value from next_cursor. Example: GET /v2/sites?page_size=200&cursor=eyJpZCI6MTIzfQ==.
  4. Repeat step 3, always using the next_cursor from the most recent response, until has_more returns false. Do not store or construct cursors manually; they expire after 15 minutes of inactivity.
  5. Aggregate your results across all pages in your application layer. Do not rely on record order across separate cursor sessions, as new records may be inserted between requests.

Troubleshooting

Error CURSOR_EXPIRED (HTTP 400): Your cursor was unused for more than 15 minutes or was malformed. Restart pagination from the first request with no cursor parameter.

Error INVALID_PAGE_SIZE (HTTP 422): Your page_size value is outside the 1–500 range. Adjust the parameter and retry.

Duplicate records across pages: This can occur if you reuse an old cursor after your access token was refreshed. Always pair a new token with a fresh pagination session.

Unexpectedly low total_records: Collection endpoints respect your OAuth2 scope's site permissions. If you expect more records, verify your token's granted scopes in the Developer Portal under Apps > Your App > Scopes. For report-specific pagination details, see How to Configure Report Schedules via the Partner API.

Title: Prepare Your Home for Inspection Day
Summary: Follow these steps before your municipal inspection appointment to ensure the inspector has safe, unobstructed access and your system passes on the first visit.
Procedure_Body__c:
Before you begin: Brightline will send an inspection confirmation notification in the Brightline Home app (under My Project > Permits > Upcoming Inspections) at least 48 hours before your scheduled date. Your inspection window is typically 4 hours (e.g., 8 a.m.–12 p.m.). An adult 18 or older must be present for the full window. If you need to reschedule, do so at least 24 hours in advance to avoid a $75 rescheduling fee charged to your account.

  1. Open Brightline Home, tap My Project, then tap Permits to confirm the inspection date, time window, and the name of the assigned municipal inspector.
  2. Clear a 3-foot path from your front door to your main electrical panel. Remove vehicles, storage bins, or equipment blocking the panel door or the area beneath your solar array.
  3. Locate and set aside any documentation the inspector may request: your Brightline installation completion certificate (available under My Project > Documents), the permit placard, and your interconnection approval letter.
  4. Ensure your Brightline gateway device has a solid green LED. If it shows amber or red, restart it by unplugging it for 30 seconds and reconnecting. A green light confirms the monitoring system is online, which the inspector will verify remotely.
  5. If you have a battery storage unit, leave it in Auto mode—do not manually force it to charge or discharge on inspection day, as the inspector will test automatic transfer switch behavior.
  6. On inspection day, greet the inspector at the scheduled start of your window and guide them to the electrical panel, attic access (if applicable), and roof access point.
  7. After the inspection, check My Project > Permits within 2 business days for your pass/fail result and next steps toward interconnection.

Troubleshooting

Inspector did not arrive within my window. Wait until 30 minutes past the end of your window, then call Brightline Support at 1-800-555-2477. Do not leave the property before calling; departing early is recorded as a missed inspection and may incur the $75 rescheduling fee.

Inspection failed due to a wiring discrepancy. Brightline will contact you within 1 business day to schedule a remediation visit at no charge if the issue originated from our installation. A re-inspection will then be booked automatically.

Gateway shows amber on inspection day. Follow the steps in How Do I Troubleshoot a Microinverter That Will Not Come Back Online for connectivity guidance, or call Support so a technician can push a remote reset before the inspector arrives.

Title: How are prorated charges handled when I change my billing date?
Summary: Changing your monthly billing date creates a one-time short or extended billing cycle with a prorated charge or credit to bridge the gap.
Answer__c:
What Happens When You Change Your Billing Date

Brightline Solar allows one billing-date change every 12 months at no fee. When you submit the change, our system closes your current billing cycle early and opens a new cycle that ends on your chosen date going forward. This creates a single transition invoice that covers the days between your old cycle-end and your new cycle-start.

Two Possible Transition Scenarios

ScenarioTransition PeriodResult
Moving billing date earlier (e.g., 15th → 1st)Less than 30 daysShort-cycle prorated charge for those days
Moving billing date later (e.g., 1st → 15th)More than 30 daysExtended-cycle invoice; net amount is still prorated per day, so you pay more once but less often initially

Example: Moving from the 15th to the 1st

Suppose your plan is $29.99/month and today is June 15. Your next normal invoice would have been July 15. Instead, we close the cycle on July 1—a 16-day period: ($29.99 ÷ 30) × 16 = $15.99. From August 1 onward, you receive standard full-month invoices on the 1st.

How to Request a Billing Date Change

  1. Open Brightline Home and navigate to Account → Billing → Billing Preferences.
  2. Tap Change Billing Date and select your preferred date (available options: 1st, 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, or 25th).
  3. Review the transition invoice preview and tap Confirm.

The transition invoice is issued within 2 business days and is due 21 days after issuance. If you are enrolled in the Brightline Hardship Program and a billing-date change would create a hardship, contact support before confirming—see Hardship Program Expansion: Extended Deferral (January 2026) for deferral options. For general information on refund timing if a credit results from your transition, see Refund Processing Time Update (Payments 2025).

Title: How does Brightline apply a partial payment when I have multiple invoices or fees?

Answer__c:
Payment Application Order

When a partial payment is received, Brightline applies funds in the following fixed priority order:

  1. Outstanding late fees – any assessed 1.5% monthly late fees are cleared first.
  2. Oldest past-due invoice balance – the invoice with the earliest original due date is paid down next.
  3. Subsequent past-due invoices – additional aged balances are paid in chronological order.
  4. Current (not yet due) invoice balance – any remaining funds are applied last.

This order is automatic and cannot be manually overridden at this time. If you need a specific allocation, you must pay each invoice individually using the custom amount field on the per-invoice payment screen (Billing → [Invoice] → Make a Payment → Enter a custom amount).

Viewing Payment Allocation

To see exactly how your payment was distributed:

  • Go to Billing → Payment History.
  • Tap the payment entry to expand the Allocation Breakdown panel, which lists each invoice or fee credited and the exact dollar amount applied.

This breakdown is also included in the emailed receipt sent within 15 minutes of payment processing.

If a payment was applied in a way that seems incorrect—for example, to a fee you believe was already waived—you can open a billing dispute in-app under Billing → Help → Dispute a Charge. Resolutions are typically issued within 5 business days.

Title: How do idempotency keys behave when a Partner API request fails or is retried?
Summary: Describes exactly how Brightline's Partner API stores, matches, and responds to retried requests that carry an idempotency key, including edge cases and error scenarios.
Answer__c:
How the Server Processes a Keyed Request

When Brightline's API receives a request with an Idempotency-Key header, it checks its deduplication store for a record matching that key plus the authenticated OAuth2 client ID. This means keys are namespaced per client—two different partners can use the same key string without conflict.

Possible Outcomes on Retry

First-request resultRetry behavior
Success (2xx)Returns the cached response body and original HTTP status. No action repeated.
Client error (4xx)Returns the same cached error. The request is not retried on the server.
Server error (5xx) or no response recordedRequest is treated as new and executed again.

Important Edge Cases

  • Mismatched request body: If you reuse a key but change the request payload, the API returns HTTP 409 with error code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT. Always keep the body identical on retries.
  • Concurrent requests: Sending two requests with the same key simultaneously returns HTTP 409 with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT. Wait for the first to complete before retrying.
  • Expired keys: Keys older than 72 hours are purged. A request with an expired key is treated as a brand-new operation.

Recommended Retry Strategy

  1. Generate a UUID v4 key before the first attempt.
  2. Retry only on network errors or 5xx responses.
  3. Use exponential back-off: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, up to 5 attempts.

For details on how webhook deliveries interact with retry logic, see Webhook Retry Policy Update – Partner API March 2026.

Send a POST request to /v2/reports/schedules with a JSON body. Required fields are shown in the table below:

FieldTypeRequiredDescription

Title: How accurate is my production estimate, and what factors affect it?
Summary: Explains how Brightline calculates production estimates, the typical accuracy range, and the key variables that can cause your actual output to differ.
Answer__c:
How Brightline Builds Your Production Estimate

Your production estimate is generated at the time of system design using a combination of your roof's pitch, azimuth, and shading profile, your local historical solar irradiance data (sourced from a 20-year weather dataset), and the rated output of your specific panel and inverter models. The result is a modeled annual figure—for most systems, within ±8% of actual output under typical conditions.

Common Reasons for a Wider Gap

  • Weather variability: A cloudier-than-average year in your area can reduce generation by 5–12% on its own.
  • Shading changes: Tree growth, new structures, or seasonal shadows not present during your site survey.
  • System downtime: Inverter faults, microinverter outages, or grid outages reduce cumulative output. Check the Alerts tab in Brightline Home for any recorded events.
  • Panel soiling: Heavy pollen seasons or bird activity can cut output 2–4% if panels haven't been cleaned.
  • Temperature extremes: Panels lose roughly 0.35% efficiency per °C above 25°C (77°F), so unusually hot summers affect totals.

What to Do If the Gap Seems Too Large

If your actual output is more than 10% below your estimate after accounting for the factors above, contact Brightline Support to request a Performance Variance Review. A technician will audit your monitoring data and flag any hardware issues. You can also review your full estimate breakdown in the app—see How to view and download your production estimate report for step-by-step instructions.

For a deeper look at specific time periods covered in your report, see What time periods are covered in my production estimate report.

Title: Handle Pagination in Partner API Webhook Backfill Requests
Summary: How to use the Partner API's offset-based pagination on the webhook event log endpoint to backfill missed events after a delivery outage.
Procedure_Body__c:
Prerequisites: Your application must have a registered webhook endpoint in the Developer Portal and an OAuth2 token with the read:events scope. This procedure covers the GET /v2/webhooks/events endpoint, which uses offset-based (not cursor-based) pagination because the event log is immutable and time-ordered. Use this workflow only to recover missed events; do not use it as a substitute for real-time delivery.

  1. Identify the time window you need to backfill. Note the UTC timestamp of the last successfully processed event stored in your system; you will use this as your starting boundary.
  2. Make an initial request to GET /v2/webhooks/events with the following query parameters: after (ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of your last processed event), before (current UTC time or desired end boundary), and limit (integer, 1–200; default 50). Example: GET /v2/webhooks/events?after=2026-03-01T00:00:00Z&before=2026-03-02T00:00:00Z&limit=200.
  3. The response includes a top-level meta object with total, offset, and limit fields, plus a data array of event objects each containing an event_id, event_type, delivered_at, and payload.
  4. Process all events in the data array in ascending delivered_at order to preserve event sequence. Record the highest delivered_at value you successfully process.
  5. If offset + limit < total, increment your next request's offset parameter by the value of limit. Example: add &offset=200 to fetch the next page.
  6. Repeat steps 4–5 until offset + limit >= total. Resume normal webhook delivery once backfill is complete.

Troubleshooting

Error INVALID_TIME_RANGE (HTTP 422): The after value is later than before, or the window exceeds 30 days. Narrow your time range to 30 days or less per request and chain multiple requests for longer outages.

Error SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT (HTTP 403): Your token is missing the read:events scope. Re-authorize your application in the Developer Portal under Apps > Your App > Edit Scopes.

Missing events in backfill window: The event log retains records for 90 days. Events older than 90 days are permanently purged and cannot be recovered via this endpoint.

SDK helpers: The official SDKs include a backfill_events() convenience method that handles offset incrementing automatically. Upgrade to the latest SDK version before using it; see Partner API SDK v2 Breaking Changes – March 2026 for migration notes. For details on real-time alert event payloads, see Temperature Warning Alerts – Partner API Endpoint Launch.

Ground-Mount Permits Are Different from Rooftop Permits

Yes — ground-mount systems require a separate and generally more complex permit package than rooftop installations. Because a ground-mount involves excavation, concrete footings, and a freestanding structure, most jurisdictions treat it as both an electrical permit and a structural/building permit, and some counties also require a grading or land-disturbance permit if more than 50 square feet of soil is disturbed.

What Brightline Submits on Your Behalf

Your Brightline project coordinator handles all permit applications. The standard ground-mount permit package includes:

  • Structural engineering stamp for the racking system (PE-stamped drawings, required in 38 of the 50 states we serve)
  • Electrical single-line diagram
  • Soil report summary if the jurisdiction requires it
  • Zoning compliance letter, where applicable

Typical Timeline

Ground-mount permit approval averages 4–8 weeks, compared to 1–3 weeks for rooftop permits. Jurisdictions with an HOA overlay or agricultural zoning can extend this to 10–12 weeks. Your Brightline Home app will show real-time permit status under My Project → Permits & Approvals.

Fees

Most permit fees are included in your Brightline installation contract. If a jurisdiction charges an additional structural review fee above $350, Brightline will notify you before submission and itemize the charge. Title: Diagnose and Fix Webhook Authentication Failures in the Partner API
Summary: Use this procedure to identify and correct authentication failures on inbound Brightline Partner API webhooks, including invalid signature errors, mismatched secrets, and rejected endpoint responses.
Procedure_Body__c:
Prerequisites: You must have at least one webhook subscription configured in the Partner Developer Portal under Webhooks > Manage Subscriptions. Your receiving endpoint must be reachable over HTTPS with a valid TLS certificate. You should have access to your server logs to inspect raw request headers. Familiarity with HMAC-SHA256 signature verification is assumed.

  1. Locate the failed delivery in the Portal. Go to Webhooks > Delivery Logs. Each delivery attempt shows the event type, HTTP status your endpoint returned, the X-Brightline-Signature-256 header value sent, and a Delivery-ID. Filter by status Failed to find recent errors.
  2. Identify the failure category. Brightline classifies webhook authentication failures into three types: SIG_MISMATCH (your endpoint rejected the signature), ENDPOINT_AUTH_REJECTED (your server returned 401 or 403), and TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED (Brightline could not establish a secure connection).
  3. Resolve SIG_MISMATCH errors. Brightline signs each webhook payload using HMAC-SHA256 with the Webhook Signing Secret shown in Webhooks > Manage Subscriptions > [Subscription Name] > Security. To verify: (a) retrieve the raw request body as bytes before any parsing, (b) compute HMAC-SHA256(signingSecret, rawBody), (c) compare the result to the value in the X-Brightline-Signature-256 header using a constant-time comparison function. A mismatch almost always means the signing secret in your code is stale — copy the current value directly from the Portal and update your environment.
  4. Resolve ENDPOINT_AUTH_REJECTED errors. If your receiving endpoint requires its own authentication (e.g., a bearer token in the request or an IP allowlist), ensure Brightline's delivery IP ranges are permitted. Current egress IP ranges are listed in the Portal under Webhooks > Delivery Settings > Egress IPs. Update your allowlist and re-enable the subscription.
  5. Resolve TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED errors. Confirm your endpoint's TLS certificate is valid, not self-signed, and covers the exact hostname registered in the Portal. Brightline requires TLS 1.2 or higher. You can test connectivity using the Send Test Event button in the Portal, which returns a detailed error message for TLS failures.
  6. Rotate the signing secret if it was exposed. In the Portal, go to Webhooks > Manage Subscriptions > [Subscription Name] > Security > Rotate Secret. During rotation, Brightline sends both the old and new signatures for a 24-hour grace period so you can deploy your update without downtime. Accept either valid signature during that window.
  7. Trigger a backfill of missed events. Once authentication is restored, you can request redelivery of failed events. See How to Handle Pagination in Partner API Webhook Backfill Requests for step-by-step instructions on retrieving missed payloads in order.

Troubleshooting

Signature still mismatches after updating the secret: Confirm you are reading the raw request body. Middleware that parses JSON before your verification handler will alter the byte sequence and invalidate the signature. Disable body pre-parsing for the webhook route. Deliveries stop after secret rotation: The 24-hour dual-signature grace period begins at the moment you click Rotate Secret; if your deployment takes longer than 24 hours, the old signature will no longer be accepted — rotate again and deploy immediately. Test events succeed but live events fail: Check that your production endpoint URL matches the registered URL exactly, including trailing slashes. Repeated failures trigger subscription suspension: Brightline suspends a subscription after 50 consecutive failed deliveries; re-enable it from the Portal after fixing the underlying issue. For details on retry timing and backoff behavior, see Webhook Retry Policy Update – Partner API March 2026. If the issue is unresolved, submit a ticket via Help > Contact Partner Support and include the Delivery-ID values from the failed attempts.

Title: Configure False Alarm Suppression Rules in Brightline Home
Summary: Set up automatic suppression rules so Brightline Home stops generating repeated false alarms for known, recurring non-issue conditions on your system.
Procedure_Body__c:
Before you begin: You must be the account owner with full Alert Management permissions. Suppression rules are available on Brightline Home app version 4.5.0 or later. Rules apply only to the site associated with your account; households with multiple sites must configure rules per site. Note that suppression rules cannot be applied to any alert with a Critical (ALT-5xx) or Safety (ALT-6xx) code.

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Settings (gear icon, top-right corner), then select Alerts & Notifications.
  2. Tap Suppression Rules, then tap Add New Rule.
  3. In the Alert Type field, search for or browse to the alert code you want to suppress — for example, ALT-204: Low Production Warning. Only alert codes that have been triggered at least once on your system appear in this list.
  4. Under Trigger Condition, define when the rule applies. Choose one or more conditions:
    • Time window — suppress the alert only between specified hours (for example, 07:00–09:00 to ignore early-morning shading alerts).
    • Duration threshold — suppress only if the alert clears automatically within a set number of minutes (2–30 minutes).
    • Repeat frequency — suppress if the same code fires more than a specified number of times within a rolling 7-day window.
  5. Set the Rule Expiry date. Rules must have an end date; the maximum is 180 days. You can renew a rule before it expires.
  6. Tap Save Rule. A confirmation banner appears: Suppression rule activated. Matching alerts will be logged silently under Alert History.
  7. To review suppressed alerts at any time, go to Alerts > Alert History and toggle the Show Suppressed filter to On.

Troubleshooting

The alert code I want to suppress is not listed. Suppression rules can only be created for alert codes your system has previously generated. If you are trying to prevent a future alert type, contact Brightline Support to discuss whether a system-wide sensitivity adjustment is appropriate for your installation.

Suppressed alerts are still sending push notifications. Suppression rules silence in-app alert cards but do not automatically disable push notifications configured under Settings > Notifications > Push Preferences. Disable the corresponding notification toggle there to stop push alerts for the suppressed code.

My rule expired and I need to renew it. Go to Settings > Alerts & Notifications > Suppression Rules, find the expired rule (marked with a gray Expired badge), and tap Renew to extend it by up to 180 additional days. If your system's production readings are frequently triggering low-production alerts, review Why Does My Production Estimate Differ from My Actual Output to determine whether an underlying production issue — rather than a false alarm — may be causing the alerts.

Title: Can someone else provide roof access if I can't be home for my Brightline appointment?
Summary: A responsible adult (18+) can grant roof access on your behalf, provided you register them in the Brightline Home app before your appointment.
Answer__c:
Yes — A Designated Contact Can Provide Roof Access

You do not need to be personally present as long as a designated on-site contact is available to grant the technician access to your roof and any electrical panels that need to be reached. This person must be at least 18 years old and physically present for the full appointment window.

How to Register a Designated Contact

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to My Appointments.
  2. Tap the relevant appointment, then select Manage Access Contact.
  3. Enter the contact's full name and a direct phone number where they can be reached on appointment day.
  4. Tap Save Contact. You will receive a confirmation notification.

Changes must be submitted at least 24 hours before the scheduled appointment start time. Same-day changes cannot be processed through the app; call Brightline Scheduling Support at 1-833-274-5566 for urgent updates.

What Your Contact Should Know

  • They should be ready 15 minutes before the appointment window opens.
  • Technicians carry Brightline-branded ID badges — your contact may ask to see one.
  • They do not need to sign any documents unless a physical permit card must be posted; the app will notify you if this applies.

If no authorized contact is present when the technician arrives, the visit will be marked as a missed access event and a rescheduling fee of $75 may apply. For more on what to have ready before the crew arrives, see What do I need to do to prepare roof access for my Brightline appointment?

Title: Can I set a different language for my email notifications than the app display?
Summary: Explains how Brightline Home handles language settings separately for the app interface and outgoing email or SMS notifications.
Answer__c:
App Language vs. Notification Language

Yes — Brightline Home keeps your app display language and your notification language as two independent settings. Changing one does not automatically change the other.

How to Set Your Notification Language

Follow these steps to update the language used for email and SMS notifications:

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to Profile → Notifications → Notification Preferences.
  2. Tap Notification Language at the top of the screen.
  3. Select your preferred language from the same list of six supported languages.
  4. Tap Save Changes.

Changes take effect for all notifications sent after you save. Notifications already queued (within the next 15 minutes) may still arrive in the previous language.

Which Notifications Are Affected

Notification TypeSupports Language Setting
Production alertsYes
Billing & payment remindersYes
Temperature warning alertsYes
Outage & system status updatesYes

Tip

If you want everything in the same language, set both Display Language and Notification Language to match. For more on temperature alert notifications specifically, see Temperature Warning Alerts Now Available in Brightline Home.

Title: Can I make changes to my ground-mount system after the permit has been submitted?
Summary: Design changes after permit submission often require a permit amendment, which can reset or extend your approval timeline and may involve additional fees.
Answer__c:
Why Changes After Submission Are Complicated

Once Brightline submits your ground-mount permit package to the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ), any change to the system design — panel count, inverter model, array orientation, or foundation type — typically requires a permit amendment or a full resubmission. Ground-mount systems are especially sensitive to design changes because the structural engineering report, site plan, and setback calculations are all tied to the exact array footprint and weight load.

Common Changes and Their Impact

Change TypeLikely OutcomeAdded Wait Time
Adding 1–4 panels (same footprint)Amendment required5–15 business days
Expanding array footprintNew structural stamp + resubmission15–30 business days
Swapping inverter modelElectrical diagram update, amendment5–10 business days
Changing foundation typeFull resubmission likely20–40 business days

Amendment Fees

Brightline charges a $175 permit amendment processing fee for changes requested after initial submission. Some jurisdictions also charge their own amendment filing fee, which is passed through at cost. Both charges will appear as a line item in your Brightline Home billing summary.

How to Request a Change

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to My Project → Design.
  2. Tap Request a Design Change and describe the modification.
  3. Your project coordinator will assess permit impact within 2 business days and send a written impact summary before any amendment is filed.

To understand the full permit process for ground-mount systems, see Do I need a separate permit for a ground-mount solar system?

Title: Can I make a partial payment on my Brightline invoice?
Summary: Explains whether partial payments are accepted, how to submit one in the Brightline Home app, and what happens to the remaining balance.
Answer__c:
Partial Payments Are Accepted

Yes, Brightline Solar does accept partial payments on outstanding invoices. You can submit any amount greater than $10.00 toward a balance due without the payment being rejected. However, a partial payment does not satisfy the invoice in full, and the remaining balance will continue to accrue a 1.5% monthly late fee (applied on the 10th calendar day after the original due date) until the balance is cleared.

How to Submit a Partial Payment in Brightline Home

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap Billing in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select the invoice you want to pay, then tap Make a Payment.
  3. On the payment screen, tap Enter a custom amount and type the amount you wish to pay.
  4. Choose your payment method and tap Submit Payment.

You will receive an email and in-app receipt within 15 minutes confirming the amount applied. The invoice detail screen will update to show the new remaining balance, marked as Partially Paid.

Will a Partial Payment Prevent Account Suspension?

A partial payment reduces your balance but does not automatically pause suspension proceedings. If your account is already in a past-due state, contact Brightline Support at 1-800-555-0192 or chat in-app to set up a payment arrangement. Customers facing financial hardship may also qualify for deferred billing through our assistance program.

See also: Brightline Hardship Program and Account Suspension Policy.

Title: Can I get receipts emailed automatically for every Brightline payment?
Summary: Explains how to enable automatic email receipts for every payment processed through Brightline Home.
Answer__c:
Enabling Automatic Payment Receipts

Yes — Brightline Home can send you an email receipt automatically every time a payment is successfully processed, whether it's a scheduled autopay, a one-time manual payment, or a retry after a previously failed charge.

How to turn on automatic receipts

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select Billing & Payments, then tap Notification Preferences.
  3. Under the Receipt Emails section, toggle Send receipt after every successful payment to On.
  4. Confirm the email address shown is correct. To change it, tap Edit Email and save.

What the receipt includes

  • Payment confirmation number (format: BL-RCT-XXXXXXXX)
  • Payment date, amount, and method (e.g., ACH, credit card ending in ····4821)
  • Invoice number(s) the payment was applied to
  • Your account balance after the payment

Receipt delivery timing

Receipts are generated and emailed within 5 minutes of a successful payment. If a payment is settled overnight (common for ACH), the receipt arrives by 6:00 AM local time the following business day.

If you're not receiving receipts even with the toggle enabled, check your spam folder for emails from receipts@mail.brightlinesolar.com, then verify your notification settings are saved. For details on what to do if a receipt shows an unexpected amount, see Why does my payment receipt show a different amount than I expected?

Title: Can I get a revised production estimate after system changes or an expansion?
Summary: Covers when and how Brightline issues updated production estimates following panel additions, battery installs, inverter swaps, or significant shading changes.
Answer__c:
When a Revised Estimate Is Issued Automatically

Brightline automatically generates a new production estimate whenever a permitted system modification is completed and passes final inspection. This includes panel expansions, full inverter replacements, and battery additions that alter your system's rated capacity. The revised estimate typically appears in Brightline Home within 3–5 business days after your utility interconnection approval is updated in our records.

You will receive an in-app notification (under Reports > Production Estimates) and an email confirming the new estimate is ready.

When You Need to Request a Revision

Some changes are not captured automatically and require a manual request:

  • Significant new shading (e.g., a neighbor's new addition or mature tree growth)
  • Panel cleaning or derating corrections after a soiling audit
  • Corrections to roof orientation data identified after installation

To submit a revision request, go to Brightline Home > Reports > Production Estimates > Request Revision and select the reason from the dropdown. A Brightline energy analyst will review your case within 7 business days and issue a revised report or contact you for a site re-assessment.

What Changes Between the Old and New Estimate

FieldOriginal EstimateRevised Estimate
System size (kW DC)Based on original designUpdated to new capacity
Annual estimate (kWh)Original modeled totalRe-modeled total
Monthly breakdownOriginal profileAdjusted seasonal profile

For information on why your revised estimate might still differ from actual output, see Why does my production estimate differ from my actual output. API users can retrieve revised estimates programmatically via Retrieve production estimates via the Partner API.

Title: Can I get a refund or credit if I was billed a prorated charge by mistake?
Summary: Describes the conditions under which Brightline will reverse or credit an incorrect prorated charge, the dispute process, and typical resolution timeframes.
Answer__c:
When a prorated charge can be reversed

Brightline will issue a correction if the prorated charge resulted from any of the following:

  • A plan change or billing-date update that was processed on the wrong date due to a system error.
  • A duplicate charge for the same billing segment.
  • An incorrect daily rate caused by a pricing configuration error on Brightline's side.
  • A service interruption of 48 hours or more that was not excluded from billing under your service agreement.

How to open a dispute

  1. In Brightline Home, go to Account → Billing → Invoice History and open the affected invoice.
  2. Tap Dispute This Charge and select the specific line item you believe is incorrect.
  3. Provide a brief description and, if available, attach a screenshot or note the date you made the plan change.
  4. Submit the form. You will receive a confirmation email with a case number (format: BL-INV-XXXXXXX) within 15 minutes.

What happens next

Brightline's billing team reviews disputes within 5–7 business days. If the charge is confirmed incorrect, you will receive either:

  • A bill credit applied to your next invoice (most common), or
  • A direct refund to your original payment method within 7–10 business days, if your account balance is zero.

Disputes must be submitted within 90 days of the invoice date; charges older than 90 days cannot be reviewed except in cases of documented system error.

For general refund timing details, see Refund processing time update. To understand refund eligibility rules more broadly, see Refund eligibility policy clarification.

Summary: Beginning April 15, 2026, Brightline Home officially supports login through Chrome for Android and Safari for iOS, with improved compatibility for in-app browsers.

This update also improves compatibility with in-app browsers embedded in email clients, resolving a class of errors where the Brightline Home login page would freeze or fail to redirect after multi-factor authentication on mobile devices.
Body__c:
Announcement Details

This release resolves error code BH-LOGIN-4031 ("OAuth redirect blocked by in-app browser") that affected users who clicked login links directly from their email apps on iOS and Android.

Title: Battery Alert Thresholds Updated for More Accurate Low-Charge Warnings

Customers can still customize these values under Settings > Alerts > Battery in the app. No action is required unless you prefer to keep your old thresholds.
